title: 149 Tiny Speakers, One Very Loud Wall
summary:
What happens if you link 149 tiny speakers together? A team at WIRED found out by building a wall of sound at its London office. The speakers were IKEA's Kallsup, a $10 Bluetooth speaker launched in April. Each one is a small cube in white, green, or pink.

WIRED asked IKEA's headquarters in Almhult if it could try. IKEA agreed and sent 150 speakers. One speaker was damaged in shipping, so the team worked with 149.

Chaining them was simple. After pairing one speaker with an iPhone 16 Pro, the team powered on another cube while music played and held down Play until a chime meant “multi-speaker” mode. Linking all the speakers took about 30 minutes.

At 100 speakers, the sound was seriously loud, like a fire alarm. At maximum volume with all 149, the team could not hear each other speak and could feel vibrations. A wall costs $1,490, and WIRED does not recommend buying one. Its lesson was simple: for high-quality audio, buy a better speaker.
why_it_matters: It helps kids see that buying more gadgets is not always better than choosing one good one.
